reuse.why: The rule changes go into the existing getScheduledAmount, which reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, and the API field calls the same helper.

duplication.why: No rule logic is copied. The inverse/return pattern is repeated in two branches inside the helper, a trivial repetition.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts and the field in scheduleModel.toExternal, but an output-only expectedAmount is added as a required field to APIScheduleEntity, which also serves as the create/update input type. That forces Omit<…, 'expectedAmount'> patches across the input signatures.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field. The input-type Omit edits are collateral of the type choice.

maintainability.why: One helper owns the rule, but op is optional and the server posting/action-sync callers (schedules/app.ts updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule) were not given it. Approximate schedules are therefore planned one way and posted another. The API entity now mixes input and output fields, and packages/api's createSchedule signature was left out.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All amount resolution goes through getScheduledAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount's rangeRounding parameter is replaced by an optional amountOp, and one isapprox branch is added. The schedules/app.ts callers still call the helper but without op, so the approximate rule is not applied there.
